findings.title: No-prefactor real-time domination fails

evidence.classification: Major (parent calibration): printed intermediate lemma is false and used in the core Bowen proof
evidence.claim: Lemma7.4(b)/(c) asserts a no-prefactor exponential F/E ratio for every real-time orbit segment outside Wr. The proof only supplies time-one domination and integer-time fake-foliation invariance; the real-time assertion is false.

exact_model.manifold: The mapping torus of the hyperbolic toral automorphism A=[[2,1],[1,1]], with identification(z,1)~(Az,0), carries the smooth unit-roof suspension flow. It is a transitive Anosov flow; the whole compact manifold is a sectional-hyperbolic invariant attractor with no singularities. If a proper attracting neighborhood is required, take its product with an independently contracting normal direction in a compact circle factor and use the invariant sink slice.
exact_model.bundles: Let lambda=(3+sqrt(5))/2 and mu=log(lambda). E is the stable eigendirection; Fcu is the flow direction plus the unstable eigendirection. Give the flow unit speed, make these directions orthogonal, and use norm weights w_s(theta)=exp(-mu theta), w_u(theta)=exp(mu theta+h(theta)), h(theta)=-6sin(2pi theta).
exact_model.gluing: w_s(theta+1)=lambda^{-1}w_s(theta), w_u(theta+1)=lambda w_u(theta), and all derivatives match the A gluing because h is smooth and1-periodic. Thus this is a globally smooth Riemannian metric, not a discontinuous fiber renormalization.
exact_model.hypotheses: Every time-one map has stable norm lambda^{-1}<1/2 and sectional area expansion lambda>1 on Fcu. The normal stable/unstable ratio gains lambda^2. Uniform estimates for arbitrary positive time retain a fixed prefactor bounded in terms of ||h||, so sectional hyperbolicity and domination hold. Orthogonality is exactly as assumed in the paper. There are no singularities, hence Wr is empty.
exact_model.contradiction: At the period-one orbit over z=0 and phase0, take t=13/12. The normal unstable/stable ratio is exp(2mu t+h(t)-h(0))=exp(13mu/6-3). Since lambda<3<exp(6/5), mu<6/5, hence this gain is below exp(-2/5)<1. Start with a small transverse displacement whose fake-foliation F/E ratio tends to11/10. At this hyperbolic return fixed point, the invariant fake stable/unstable leaves are tangent to the stable/unstable eigenspaces. Therefore the final actual ratio tends to(11/10)exp(13mu/6-3)<1; the inequality remains strict for sufficiently small nonzero displacement. Such a displacement lies in any prescribed finite-time Bowen ball after shrinking it. Lemma7.4(b) instead requires final ratio>=lambda_R^(13/12)>1.
exact_model.exact_auxiliary_bound: exp(6/5)>1+6/5+(6/5)^2/2+(6/5)^3/6=401/125>3. Also exp(2/5)>1+2/5>11/10. These prove the strict inequalities without relying on floating-point arithmetic.
exact_model.numerical_orientation_only: The ratio gain is approximately0.400617265301; this number is not the proof.

evidence.dependency: Page62 repeatedly applies Lemma7.4 to gaps (t_i^+,t_(i+1)^-) between singular visits. These are arbitrary real entry/exit intervals, even when the total good segment has integer length. Page63 then relies on large F-coordinate at each such endpoint. Thus restricting the total segment length to integers does not remove this use.
evidence.alternative_readings: The paper explicitly notes on pp54-55 that the fake foliations need not be invariant at noninteger times. No instantaneous adapted-metric hypothesis is supplied; the foundations helper independently checked pp11-35 and found only orthogonalization plus time-one estimates. A continuous-time adapted metric could change the formulation, but has not been constructed with the needed subsequent constants here.
evidence.repair_status: No complete downstream repair has been established. An integer-grid proof would need uniform end-interval constants, coordinate changes and sufficient domination margins; these must also be compatible with the singular-entry/exit lemmas. Merely adding an arbitrary constant C to7.4 does not by itself justify repeated preservation of the threshold F>=E. The final Bowen theorem is not refuted.

findings.verified_repair: No complete downstream repair. Integer estimates with bounded end constants or adapted continuous geometry require new threshold-propagation proof.
findings.impact: Used in Proposition7.2, Theorem5.1 Bowen property, TheoremC and deductions A/B.
findings.limit: Main theorems and final Bowen conclusion not refuted.

evidence.exact_mismatch: Writing t=N+r with N=floor(t), 0<=r<1, both Pliss sequences are indexed by x_(r+j), j=1,...,N. Their intersection produces a time s=r+m=t-n. It does not produce s in N unless r=0. The page-35 image confirms that the printed conclusion is s in [0,t] intersect N.

counterexample.ambient_model: Use the smooth suspension of B=A^2 on T^2 with constant roof 2, where A=[[2,1],[1,1]] and B=[[5,3],[3,2]]. The compact mapping torus identifies (z,2) with (Bz,0); the vector field is partial_theta. This is a transitive, nonsingular Anosov flow and its whole manifold is a sectional-hyperbolic attractor. In particular, its singularity set is empty.
compatibility_with_one_step_assumptions: Let lambda_A=(3+sqrt(5))/2 and alpha=log(lambda_A). In eigenvector coordinates of B, choose the smoothly descending metric with norms |v_s|_theta=e^(-alpha theta)|v_s|, |v_u|_theta=e^(alpha theta)|v_u| and |partial_theta|=1, with the three directions orthogonal.
The identifications are compatible because the eigenvalues of B are e^(-2alpha) and e^(2alpha). The flow contracts E^s by e^(-alpha t) and expands E^u by e^(alpha t).

For E=E^s and F=span(X) direct-sum E^u, the time-one domination product is e^(-alpha)=1/lambda_A<1/2, and sectional expansion on the two-dimensional F is e^alpha=lambda_A>1. Thus the normalization used in (2.3) and (2.4) is satisfied.
counterexample.choices: Let W be the open phase band theta in (0.8,1.2) modulo 2. This is an open neighborhood of the empty singularity set, as allowed by the stated quantifier. Take x on the period-2 orbit over the fixed point z=0, at phase zero, and let beta_0=1/3.
verification: For every arbitrarily large integer N, put t=N+1/2. Both x and x_t lie outside W.

For every j=0,...,floor(t)=N, the phase of x_(t-j) is either 1/2 or 3/2. Hence the sampled W-frequency in the hypothesis of Lemma 4.7 is exactly zero, and satisfies that hypothesis for every beta_1>0.
For every positive odd integer s<=t, x_s lies in W; the s=0 suffix test in Definition 11 already fails.
For every positive even integer s<=t, s>=2, and the last two sampled points x_s and x_(s-1) contain one point of W. The corresponding ratio is 1/2>beta_0, so recurrence-Pliss again fails.

Time zero is not an eligible simultaneous Pliss time under Definitions 10 and 11, which require positive duration (Definition 10 requires t>1). Thus there is no eligible integer s satisfying the conclusion, for arbitrarily large t.
Failure of recurrence alone excludes simultaneous Pliss times, independently of the choice of lambda_0.
counterexample.conclusion: The counterexample violates the literal conclusion for every possible threshold N1 associated with this fixed W. It is not merely a failure of the printed proof to establish an otherwise untested assertion.

findings.title: Pressure is not bounded by every empirical limit

core.classification: Major (parent calibration): false universal limit-point claim used in the pressure gap
core.claim: Lemma5.9 states that P(C,phi,delta)<=P_mu(phi) for any weak limit of the integer-indexed weighted empirical measures. A limsup pressure can only be recovered along an appropriate maximizing sequence, not every subsequence.
core.counterexample: Within a transitive Anosov suspension choose two disjoint periodic orbits gamma0,gamma1 and a smooth potential equal0 on gamma0 and1 on gamma1. Let C_t be the singleton{p0} when floor(t) is even and{p1} when floor(t) is odd. Every separated partition sum is then1 or e^t, so P(C,phi,delta)=1. Along even integer times the empirical measures converge to the periodic-orbit measure mu0 with entropy0 and integral0, so P_mu0=0. Thus the asserted inequality fails in the same general class of compact flows. An additional version choosing C_t={p1} only at half-integer times and{p0} at every integer shows why arbitrary real-time collections cannot automatically be sampled only at integer times.
core.local_repair: First choose real times t_j->infinity realizing the pressure limsup and near-maximal separated sets at those times; then take a weak limit of the corresponding weighted empirical measures. The entropy-block argument must retain these times and absorb the fractional final block. The applications helper checked this AppendixA modification in detail. All long-time occupancy bounds used in5.10-5.13 are bounds for every weighted empirical measure, so they apply to this chosen maximizing sequence once the separate grid/occupancy corrections are made.
core.limitation: This repairs the quantifier/limsup step, not the independent real-time Bowen lemma.

occupation.classification: Local proof correction; integrated with the pressure-gap issue rather than a claimed separate counterexample to TheoremC
occupation.observation: The p44 inference to delta_(x,t)(Wr)>beta1 ignores that the prefix is known only to lie in Wr union U_Sing, and replaces integer sampling by continuous occupancy without a quantitative residence-time loss. No separate complete dynamical counterexample to the final pressure inequality is asserted here.
occupation.repair: Assume the count in Lemma5.8 has been obtained on a consistent grid. Near each singularity |X(z)|<=L d(z,sigma). Every complete Wr visit enters the radius r0, reaches radius r, and exits radius r0, so its duration is at least2log(r0/r)/L. Shrink r at the already flexible parameter-choice step so every such visit lasts at least4. If one visit contains K integer samples and has duration ell, then K<=ell+1<=(5/4)ell. Therefore continuous middle-interval occupancy is at least(4/5) times the discrete count. Enlarge N1 to absorb floor errors and retain at least0.6 beta1 as a fraction. Prefix and suffix lie in Wr union U_Sing, so the full empirical measure has at least0.6 beta1 there. Weak limits put that mass on its closure. Subtracting the bound beta1/1000 for the part of U_Sing outside the singular balls leaves more than beta1/2, sufficient for Lemma5.4. The same complete-visit argument handles the suffix after aligning its integer phase.
occupation.status: Complete local quantitative argument conditional on the corrected grid and its discrete count; does not close the independent Bowen proof.

findings.verified_repair: Choose pressure-maximizing real t_j first; n_j=ceil(t_j) for entropy joins costs bounded potential error; flow-average the discrete limit. Occupation correction uses complete visits length>=4 and Wr union U_Sing, conditionally on coherent grid.
findings.impact: Variational passage is used for the bad-collection pressure gap.
findings.limit: Corrected local variational statement is proved; full pressure/Bowen chain not certified.

findings.title: General cone lower estimates are false

evidence.classification: Major (parent calibration): false intermediate inequality; local replacement and bounded downstream impact established
evidence.claim: The unconditional lower bound |y^2|-L0 alpha|y^1|<=|yF| in Lemma6.1 is false for every proposed L0, even in R2.
evidence.counterexample: Let E be the horizontal axis and F the vertical axis. For every a=alpha>0 choose y=(0,1), yF=(a/(1+a^2),1/(1+a^2)), y-yF=(-a/(1+a^2),a^2/(1+a^2)). Both cone inequalities hold with equality. Yet |yF|=1/sqrt(1+a^2)<1 while the printed lower bound is1-L0*a*0=1. Swapping the roles of E and F gives the symmetric failure. The example persists for arbitrarily small alpha.
evidence.general_replacement: Write yF=(p,q), y-yF=(r,s) with |p|<=alpha|q| and |s|<=alpha|r|. Then |y^2|<=|q|+alpha|r|<=(1+alpha^2)|yF|+alpha|y^1|. Hence |yF|>=(|y^2|-alpha|y^1|)/(1+alpha^2), and symmetrically |y-yF|>=(|y^1|-alpha|y^2|)/(1+alpha^2). The printed upper estimates remain obtainable for small alpha.
evidence.complete_conditional_repair: Put A=|yF|,B=|y-yF| and assume A>=C0 B. Then |y^2|<=A+alpha B<=(1+alpha/C0)A, and |y^2|>=A/sqrt(1+alpha^2)-alpha B>=A(1/sqrt(1+alpha^2)-alpha/C0). Therefore A is within1+O(alpha) of|y^2|, with constants depending on fixed C0 as allowed. Also |y^1|<=alpha A+B<=(alpha+1/C0)A, giving |y^2|>=C0(1-C0'alpha)|y^1| after choosing C0' and sufficiently small alpha. Exchanging E,F proves Case(2). This proof does not use the false general lower bound.
evidence.downstream: Lemma6.4 on p51 uses only Cases(1)/(2) with fixed C0=.8,1.8,1/3 plus the graph arc-length comparison Lemma6.3. The repaired conditional comparisons preserve its contradiction (.8*1.8>1) and its1+O(alpha) coordinate bounds. Thus this local coordinate-change application survives. The applications helper separately checked the AppendixB derivation; no independent AppendixB reading by this helper is claimed.

findings.verified_repair: General denominator1+alpha^2 lower bound and1+O(alpha) conditional Cases are proved independently in report.
findings.impact: Invalid derivation of coordinate tool in core geometric argument; Lemma6.4's needed conditional comparison survives.
findings.limit: No counterexample to conditional Cases or main theorem.

findings.title: Time-change potential must not be replaced by absolute value

evidence.title: The time-rescaling footnote incorrectly replaces the potential by its absolute value
evidence.status: Established local formula error; directly repairable
evidence.proposed_severity: Minor local correction; final calibration by parent
correct_identity: For c>0 and the accelerated flow g_t=f_(ct), the spaces of flow-invariant probability measures agree.
For every such mu, h_mu(g_1)=c h_mu(f_1). Therefore h_mu(g_1)+integral c phi dmu = c(h_mu(f_1)+integral phi dmu).
Consequently P_g(c phi)=c P_f(phi) and the equilibrium-state sets coincide. The absolute value is absent from this identity.
background_compatible_counterexample: Use a three-dimensional transitive Anosov suspension, which is within the nonsingular sectional-hyperbolic setting, and choose two distinct periodic orbits gamma_0 and gamma_1. For the explicit suspension in FND-01, B has five fixed points, so two such suspension orbits are available.
Let H=h_top(f_1)<infinity and choose a smooth potential phi with -K<=phi<=0, phi=0 on gamma_0, phi=-K on gamma_1, where K>2H.
The periodic orbit measure on gamma_0 gives P(phi)>=0. For any equilibrium state mu of phi, h_mu+integral phi=P(phi)>=0 implies integral phi>=-h_mu>=-H.
The periodic orbit measure on gamma_1 gives P(-phi)>=K. For any equilibrium state nu of -phi, h_nu-integral phi=P(-phi)>=K implies integral phi<=h_nu-K<=H-K<-H.
Thus the equilibrium-state sets for phi and -phi are disjoint. Their existence follows from entropy expansivity/upper semicontinuity in this Anosov setting, also recalled in the manuscript.
Because phi<=0, the printed |c phi| equals -c phi. Its equilibrium states for the accelerated flow are exactly those of -phi for the original flow, and hence differ from those of phi.
evidence.repair_and_limit: Replace |c phi| by c phi. Since c is positive, the required singularity inequalities phi(sigma)<P(phi) scale to c phi(sigma)<P_g(c phi), preserving the pressure gap. This finding is not a counterexample to the main uniqueness claim.

findings.verified_repair: Replace |c phi| with c phi for c>0; entropy, pressure and singularity gap scale exactly.
findings.impact: Local normalization formula; correct flow-invariant equilibrium sets restored.

findings.title: Finite entrance hypothesis missing

evidence.title: Lemma 2.16 needs a finite backward entrance-time hypothesis
evidence.proposed_severity: Minor limitation of the stated domain; final calibration by parent

anchors.location: Lemma 2.16 quantifies over every x in B_r(sigma) intersect Lambda and then uses x_(-t_x)

witness: The quantified set includes x=sigma. Its backward orbit stays in B_(r0)(sigma) for all time, so t_x=infinity and x_(-t_x) is not a defined finite-time orbit point on the boundary.

The issue is not restricted to the singular point. A sectional-hyperbolic attractor containing sigma contains its local unstable manifold. For a nonzero point x sufficiently near sigma on W^u_loc(sigma), the entire negative orbit stays in B_(r0)(sigma) and converges to sigma, again giving t_x=infinity.
Interpreting an infinite-time limit would yield sigma, which is not on the asserted boundary, so it would not make the displayed conclusion valid.
evidence.correction: Restrict the entry assertion to regular points with finite backward exit/entrance time t_x<infinity (equivalently, exclude the local unstable branch for a sufficiently small isolating neighborhood). In the displayed boundary, the center should be sigma rather than the printed x.
evidence.impact_limit: Finite passages of a good orbit from outside W_r back to outside W_r have the needed finite entrance. The correction does not refute the center-cone assertion for those actual passages, or the main theorem.

findings.verified_repair: Require finite t_x and use sphere centered at sigma.
findings.impact: Rules out undefined infinite backward entrance; good finite completed passages satisfy intended condition.
findings.limit: Finite-passage center-cone result and main theorem not refuted.

independent_acceptance_review.performing_role: Current acceptance root; independent focused mathematical verification
independent_acceptance_review.scope: Independent verification of all seven reported findings and their repairs/limits, including the actual smooth dynamical witnesses, continuous versus integer time quantifiers, pressure-subsequence argument, cone estimates, and reported local proof completions. Current root read the complete report, findings and coverage and 24 decisive source pages; original 96-page coverage remains historical and is not relabelled as a new full-paper verification.

findings.reason: The metric weights descend smoothly through the A mapping-torus gluing, preserve orthogonality and all printed time-one conditions, and retain uniform-prefactor sectional hyperbolicity at real times. At the phase-zero periodic orbit, the ratio factor at 13/12 is exp(13mu/6-3)<exp(-2/5)<1. The fake invariant leaves at the hyperbolic time-one return have the stable/unstable tangent directions; shrinking a displacement of initial ratio near 11/10 makes the actual final ratio <1 while satisfying any fixed finite-time Bowen scale. The nonsingular setting is admitted. Source pp.54-55 expressly give only integer invariance, and p.62 actually uses arbitrary singular exit-entry gaps. This is a false core intermediate assertion; no completed continuous-time threshold-propagation repair or main uniqueness counterexample is claimed.

The roof-two Anosov suspension with smooth exponential metric has the required one-step constants. For W phase band (0.8,1.2), t=N+1/2, all endpoint-grid samples are at phases 1/2 or 3/2 and meet the hypothesis with zero bad frequency. Every odd integer candidate lies in W; every positive even integer has frequency 1/2 in its last two samples, exceeding beta0<1/2. Duration zero is ineligible. Thus the printed integer-output lemma fails for arbitrarily large t. The common t-Z grid and strict density slack give the local correction, but the real duration s-p need not belong to the integer-defined G_B. That independent interface remains unresolved.

findings.decision: retain Major with bounded variational repair
findings.reason: Alternating singleton collections on two periodic orbits with potential values 0 and 1 give pressure limsup 1 and a legitimate empirical subsequential limit of measure pressure 0. Choosing the high orbit only at noninteger times also disproves automatic replacement of real-time pressure by integer sampling for an arbitrary collection. Selecting maximizing real t_j first, using ceil(t_j) partition joins, and absorbing the bounded potential tail gives the entropy inequality; flow-averaging the discrete limit preserves entropy by affinity/conjugacy and the potential integral. Continuous occupation requires the stated union of neighborhoods and long-complete-visit loss. Its >beta1/2 margin is valid conditionally on coherent discrete counts; this does not finish the independent Bowen/grid repair.

findings.decision: retain Major with conditional cases repaired
findings.reason: The vectors y=(0,1), u=(a,1)/(1+a^2), v=y-u satisfy both exact cones and Appendix B norm bounds, yet |u|<1 while the asserted lower bound equals 1. The missing term cannot be absorbed when y^1=0. The general denominator 1+a^2 and upper estimate follow by two projection inequalities. Under fixed A>=C0 B, direct projection yields a positive 1/sqrt(1+a^2)-a/C0 coefficient and therefore the needed 1+O_C0(a) bounds. The p.51 coordinate application uses those repairable conditional cases, not a demonstrated false final conclusion.

For positive time scaling the entropy and signed potential c*phi both scale by c. A negative smooth potential supported between two periodic orbit values and amplitude B>2h_top makes equilibrium states for phi and -phi disjoint via the report's exact entropy bounds. The absolute value in the printed footnote is therefore false; deleting it restores this normalization and the singularity pressure gap.

A=b2>b1 forces theta0=1, so strictly more than N indices are impossible. At t=1 only one positive recurrence endpoint is eligible, contradicting kappa(floor(t)+1)>1 for kappa>1/2. Non-strict/floor counts or smaller fixed density with a large-time cutoff repair these endpoints. They do not cure the separate phase mismatch.

The quantified x=sigma has infinite backward stay time, making x_-tx undefined; a regular local unstable point gives the same issue. Requiring finite entrance and centering the sphere at sigma recovers the finite completed-passage scope used later. Infinite-time limits do not land on that boundary.

The stable leg in (7.16) is y^F to y, as the product-coordinate definition requires. The speed factor cancels in the Holder/time-change sum after scaled shadowing is assumed. In finite specification, choosing the initial disk on the actual stable-plaque intersection and composing inverse branches in reverse order evaluates each transition once; this is consistent with the checked source formulas. Named disk/inclination, Tucker, CT and Appendix C off-attractor/real-time inputs remain outside a complete new reconstruction. The source's date discrepancy and exact version are preserved.

limitations: Exact arXiv:2209.10784v3, including distinct margin and internal dates, only.
